clue.text: Dog is furiously vociferous, given dehydrated food

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
someone who rants is shouting furiously

explanation.surface: A dog barks wildly when handed a bowl of dried food.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small dried grapes, a classic dried fruit used in baking.

clue.text: Twin helping the furniture remover

definitions.meaning: one of the Heavenly Twins of Greek myth, brother of Pollux
a small swivelling wheel fitted to a chair or table leg makes it easy to shift

explanation.surface: One twin lends a hand to a removal man.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are spelt alike: the mythical twin and the little wheel under furniture that aids moving it.

clue.text: Spike thrust through crimson rose

indicators.note: one piece is pushed into the middle of the other, so the colour word is pierced by the spike

parts.note: crimson is a shade of red
an ear is the spike of grain on a cereal plant

explanation.surface: A thorn pierces a deep red rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like the flower but is the past tense of rise, matching 'reared' as in rose up.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that rears or a building that is raised has gone up, so the past tense means stood up high.

clue.text: Peep at it to stir desire

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters of these three words are mixed

explanation.surface: Peeking at something tempting arouses longing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunger or a strong wish for something is the usual synonym for this craving.

clue.text: Red wine's in the marqueé

definitions.meaning: a deep red Spanish wine, once used as communion wine
a marquee is a large canvas shelter put up for parties

explanation.surface: The claret is being served under the canvas at the party.
explanation.definitionFit: The same spelling names a dark Spanish wine and a canvas shelter, of which a marquee is a large example.

clue.text: Metal drawer

parts.note: read not as a steel drawer in a desk but as something that draws iron towards itself

explanation.surface: A steel drawer in a filing cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: This object attracts iron, so it literally draws metal to it.

clue.text: A secondary route out of the country

parts.note: in Britain ... is a secondary road, below an A road in the classification

explanation.surface: Taking a minor road to leave the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: British roads are classed A (main) and B (secondary); a B road is a lesser route.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overseas or in a foreign land means being outside one's own country.

clue.text: No cure it appears, unfortunately, for deviant

indicators.note: the unlucky outcome is the letters of the three words knocked into disorder

explanation.surface: Sadly there seems to be no remedy for a pervert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears' is only a link joining the fodder to the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychologically abnormal or anxious behaviour departs from the norm, so a deviant can be described this way.

clue.text: Order canned fish — essential starters

annotationWithheld.why: Order canned fish — essential starters (8): the only parse found is ID inside TIN plus ESS, where 'canned' must give TIN and also signal the containment (one word, two jobs), and ESS as 'essential starters' is unsupported

clue.text: Gang on mud strip — abandoning favourite pitch

indicators.note: the letters abandon their order and are rearranged with wild abandon

explanation.surface: A gang leaves a muddy strip of ground for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' suggests a sports field, keeping the mud and gang in the picture, but it means a place one habitually frequents.
explanation.definitionFit: A favourite haunt, the place someone regularly goes, is their usual pitch.

clue.text: See 9
Reunion, we hear, with old naval hero

indicators.note: the word for a gathering is spoken, and the entry is spelt like something that sounds the same

parts.note: a rally is a mass gathering or reunion

explanation.surface: A gathering of veterans to honour a former admiral.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Walter Raleigh, Elizabethan explorer and sea captain, whose name is often pronounced like 'rally'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter, the Elizabethan seafarer and courtier, is a famous English sailor of old.

clue.text: Topping sole consumed with salt

indicators.note: to top something is to cut off its head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: consumed means ate

explanation.surface: Sprinkling salt over a fish dish that has been eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a chemical salt or ester of oleic acid, found in soaps.

clue.text: Account in the red? That takes the biscuit!

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, the account placed within the colour

parts.note: maroon is a dark brownish red

explanation.surface: Being overdrawn at the bank really is the last straw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That takes the biscuit' is the idiom for an outrage, but here it just points to the definition 'biscuit'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a chewy almond or coconut confection, classed as a small cake or biscuit.

clue.text: One of Arthur's men had to support the party

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower part holds up the upper, so the second word sits beneath the first

parts.note: a gala is a festive party or celebration
taken as written

explanation.surface: A knight was obliged to back the festivities.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Galahad was a Knight of the Round Table at King Arthur's court.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad, the purest knight, sat at the Round Table of King Arthur.

clue.text: Ship master wrecked going round the point

indicators.note: the scrambled title surrounds the compass point
a ship's wreck breaks things apart, so the letters of the captain's title are rearranged

parts.note: E for east is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A captain runs his vessel aground rounding a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' makes STAMER from MASTER, and 'going round' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel driven by steam power is a type of ship.

clue.text: Epitaph on old Bob brings tears

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is carved on gravestones
a bob was a shilling in old British money, abbreviated s

explanation.surface: A gravestone for poor old Bob makes mourners weep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' suggests weeping, but it is the verb of tearing. Before decimal currency a shilling was nicknamed a bob and written s.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense: tearing cloth or paper, it rends it apart.

clue.text: All puffed up, with snake bite

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake
a sting is a bite from an insect or creature

explanation.surface: A snake rears up proudly before it strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bragging is swollen with self-importance, inflated with pride.

clue.text: Shoot dead and replace this man of the faith

parts.note: a bud is a young shoot on a plant
D is the abbreviation for dead, as on family trees

indicators.note: replacing the letters puts them in new places, rearranging the word this

explanation.surface: An instruction to kill a believer and substitute him.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the Buddha's teaching is an adherent of that religion.

clue.text: Doctor got anaesthetic for joint operation

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered

parts.note: ether was an early general anaesthetic

explanation.surface: The surgeon reached for gas before operating on a knee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' makes TOG from GOT. 'Joint operation' looks surgical, matching the doctor and anaesthetic, but means jointly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something jointly or in partnership is acting in concert, a joint effort.

clue.text: Where this, our responsibility lies

parts.note: the burden that rests upon ourselves, split into two short words, describes the very word meaning a duty

explanation.surface: A statement about where our duty rests.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden or duty rests upon someone, so this word for an obligation is where it lies.

clue.text: Managed to continue the journey in Asia

parts.note: ran means managed, as one runs a business
to go on is to keep travelling

explanation.surface: Somehow the travellers kept going through the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: The city is now called Yangon, the former capital of Myanmar (Burma).
explanation.definitionFit: The former name of Yangon, a city of Burma in South-East Asia.

clue.text: A swimmer, I thresh legs about in river

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the river abbreviation
threshing tosses the material about, so these letters are beaten into a new order

explanation.surface: A swimmer thrashing their legs around in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thresh' rearranges I and LEGS, and 'about' puts that round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A young salmon returning from the sea for the first time is a fish, a swimmer.

clue.text: It may be born or borne

definitions.meaning: a set of puppies or kittens delivered at once
a stretcher or covered couch carried by bearers

explanation.surface: Something that may be born or carried along.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a brood of young animals delivered together and a carried bed or stretcher.

clue.text: Puts in order for one's entitlements

definitions.meaning: sets upright or corrects, as one sets a capsized boat straight
what a person is entitled to by law, as in human entitlements

explanation.surface: Sorting out what a person is due.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means sets straight or corrects; the noun means just claims a person holds.

clue.text: A team not fancied yet with star quality

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
real means not imagined or fancied

explanation.surface: An underdog team that has nevertheless got stardust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not fancied' suggests an outsider in a match, but it means not imaginary.
explanation.definitionFit: This means relating to the stars, as in time measured against the fixed stars.

clue.text: Imagine dancing without a sign of 1 down with partner

indicators.note: the letters dance about into a new order
one letter of the fodder is left out of the rearrangement

explanation.surface: Picture a dance without one partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A from IMAGINE and rearrange the rest. Castor (1 down) and his twin Pollux are the Twins of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac sign of the Twins, Castor and his brother Pollux.

clue.text: She got hurt doing the twist

indicators.note: twisting the word scrambles its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman was injured dancing the twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is a fair definition by example: a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a girl's name and that of a biblical woman, so any woman will do.

clue.text: Can't be made without some dripping

definitions.text: Can't be made without some dripping

parts.words: Can't be made without some dripping
parts.note: suggests cooking fat, but describes water freezing as it drips from a ledge

explanation.surface: A recipe that needs some cooking fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanging spike of ice forms only when water drips and freezes.

clue.text: Teachers contrive to get the bird

parts.note: the NUT, National Union of Teachers, was a British teaching union
to hatch a plan is to contrive it

explanation.surface: Teachers plot to snare a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tree-climbing songbird is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Habitat of snipe?

parts.note: the wading bird points one way, but a street urchin is the snipe from the drain at the roadside

explanation.surface: Where a wading bird lives.
explanation.definitionFit: A street urchin is called a guttersnipe, so the roadside drain is where that snipe lives.

clue.text: Plans to hold Bible study classes in the cathedral

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: charts are plans or maps
RE, religious education, is the school subject of Bible study

explanation.surface: Diagrams for scripture lessons held in a great church.
explanation.walkthrough: Chartres is a French city famed for its Gothic cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartres cathedral in France is a celebrated Gothic church, standing here for the city's name.
